title: Queued -> Running -> done on commit statuses
description: Every context reads 'pending / Running' from the moment the PipelineRun starts, because set-status-pending posts description 'Running' for all contexts (github-status-reporter.ts pendingScript). Using core's new optional startStep hook (tektonic-aat): set-status-pending posts pending/'Queued' linked to the PipelineRun; startStep posts pending/'Running' linked to the TaskRun and writes the start time under /tekton/home; finalStep appends the duration ('Passed in 3m12s', 'Failed: step x exited 1 (2m05s)'). startStep must not fail the task (onError continue, like the pending task). Release once core ships the hook; widen/adjust the peer range only if required.
acceptance_criteria: Statuses show Queued until the task's pod starts, then Running, then the result with duration; tests cover the three scripts; CHANGELOG Unreleased entry; released to npm.
notes:
Parent epic: plan-ii4 (common/ hub). Blocked by tektonic-aat.
PR open: feat/ldr-queued-running. Release needs core with startStep (post-2.3.0) to show Running; reporter itself can ship any time.

title: Details links and failing-step descriptions on commit statuses
description: Commit statuses carry no target_url, so GitHub's Details link leads nowhere, and a failure reads only 'Failed'. Add a detailsUrl option (with a tektonDashboardUrl helper) that sets target_url: TaskRun for a task's own status, PipelineRun for pending and reconciled ones. Name the first failing step and its exit code in the failure description.

title: Checks API reporter that puts failure logs in GitHub
description: Commit statuses hold only state, a 140-char description and a link, so seeing why a task failed needs a reachable console. A GitHubChecksReporter would post a check run per task instead (the PAC token is a GitHub App installation token, so the Checks API is open to it), with a Markdown summary, the tail of the failing step's output and annotations. Needs a core change first: a report step cannot read another step's output, so core's script wrapper would have to tee step output to a file under /tekton/home (bounded in size) for the reporter to read. Exported through core's public surface, per this repo's compatibility rule.
notes:
2026-10-13 design expansion (tektonic GitHub integration review). Phase 2 after the Queued/Running status work.
Lifecycle: set-status-pending creates one check run per context with status queued (and details_url to the PipelineRun); start step PATCHes in_progress + started_at, details_url to the TaskRun; final step PATCHes completed with conclusion success/failure, output.title/summary (Markdown: step table, exit codes, duration) and the failing step's log tail; reconciler concludes skipped (status None) or failure/timed_out/cancelled where Tekton's reason says so.
Annotations: parse the captured log tail with a configurable regexp (same idea as PAC's error-detection-simple-regexp).
Token: must be a GitHub App installation token (PATs cannot write checks) -> PAC's {{ git_auth_secret }} via podTemplateEnv, i.e. skipTokenInjection mode.
Dependencies in core: tektonic-aat (startStep hook), tektonic-36a (pass check-run IDs from the pending task to each task), tektonic-u7b (bounded step-output capture).
To verify early: runs created with the PAC App token belong to the PAC App's check suite; GitHub's Re-run button then sends check_run.rerequested to PAC. Find out what PAC does with it (likely re-runs the whole PipelineRun) and document.
Ship as GitHubChecksReporter alongside GitHubStatusReporter, not a replacement.
Parent epic: plan-t0r (common/ hub). Blocked by tektonic-aat, tektonic-36a, tektonic-u7b.

title: Generic uploadSarifStep helper for GitHub code scanning
description: ocidex has a best-effort SARIF upload step (ocidex/.tektonic/shared.ts uploadSarifStep) that feeds GitHub's Security tab from report-only scan tasks. Lift a generic version here (image, token source, category, always exits 0) so any tektonic consumer can publish scanner findings to code scanning. Note the token needs security-events: write; a PAC App token works if the App has that permission.
